instruction: Review the segmenter training report and investigate how to minimize the kept ratio while retaining or improving downstream ASR, with particular attention to decoder-segmenter frequency bias.
scope: Adaptive compression of 50 Hz self-supervised speech features into a low-rate acoustic prefix for decoder-only ASR.
sub_questions: Does a decoder co-adapt to a particular acoustic-prefix rate or alignment?
Which constrained adaptive-compression mechanisms are more stable than independent frame Bernoulli actions?
How should output count be controlled during training?
Can multi-rate training and distillation preserve ASR under lower budgets?
How can decoder bias be separated from boundary error, positional shift, pooling shift, and true information loss?

papers.title: Variable Frame Rate Acoustic Models Using Minimum Error Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Dongcheng Jiang, Chao Zhang, Philip C. Woodland
papers.problem: Learn content-dependent frame skipping while optimizing ASR sequence error and computational rate.
papers.method: Pretrain a skip controller from phone alignments, then apply minimum-phone-error reinforcement learning with an explicit frame-rate term and a sampled-minus-baseline error.
papers.results: Variable-rate MGB3 models slightly improved both WER and rate relative to fixed low-rate baselines; the paper notes that pushing already-low rates further can trade away accuracy.
papers.relevance: Closest precedent for the current imitation-to-RL schedule; supports a matched high-rate loss baseline and explicit rate-quality optimization.

papers.title: Learning Adaptive Downsampling Encoding for Online End-to-End Speech Recognition
papers.authors: Rui Na, Junfeng Hou, Wu Guo, Yan Song, Lirong Dai
papers.problem: Replace fixed-rate speech subsampling with content-adaptive online selection.
papers.method: Optimize a differentiable expectation over hard keep decisions and add an entropy penalty to make probabilities decisive.
papers.results: Reported TIMIT PER 20.86 versus 22.44 for fixed downsampling, with robustness to speed perturbation.
papers.relevance: Provides a lower-variance alternative to REINFORCE and clarifies that entropy can be used to sharpen rather than prolong indecision.

papers.title: Trainable Dynamic Subsampling for End-to-End Speech Recognition
papers.authors: Shucong Zhang, Erfan Loweimi, Yumo Xu, Peter Bell, Steve Renals
papers.problem: Static subsampling can retain redundant frames and miss useful ones.
papers.method: A dynamic-subsampling RNN learns a binary frame-skip controller jointly with an attention-based ASR model.
papers.results: Reported TIMIT PER 16.8 versus 23.5 and 20.4 for static unidirectional and bidirectional baselines.
papers.relevance: Early evidence that adaptive selection can improve accuracy rather than merely reduce compute, though only on a small RNN setup.

papers.title: End-to-end Speech Recognition with Adaptive Computation Steps
papers.authors: Mohan Li, Min Liu, Masanori Hattori
papers.problem: Dynamically determine how many acoustic frames are sufficient for each linguistic output.
papers.method: Encoder-side adaptive integration creates monotonic, label-synchronous acoustic representations.
papers.results: Reported AIShell-1 CER 31.2 online and 18.7 offline versus 32.4 and 22.0 attention baselines.
papers.relevance: Suggests accumulation into linguistic units rather than unconstrained frame-wise selection.

papers.title: CIF: Continuous Integrate-and-Fire for End-to-End Speech Recognition
papers.problem: Learn monotonic frame-to-label alignment with continuous and differentiable operations.
papers.method: Accumulate learned frame weights until an acoustic token fires; use target-length scaling and a quantity loss to control count.
papers.results: Competitive ASR; ablations show that count scaling, quantity loss, and the autoregressive decoder are all important.
papers.relevance: Strong template for differentiable count control and a token-synchronous acoustic interface.

papers.title: CTC-based Compression for Direct Speech Translation
papers.authors: Marco Gaido, Mauro Cettolo, Matteo Negri, Marco Turchi
papers.problem: Dynamically compress speech features without an external phone recognizer.
papers.method: Use CTC predictions to group consecutive frames and average or confidence-weight each group.
papers.results: Reported 1.3-1.5 BLEU gains and over 10 percent memory reduction for direct speech translation; ASR-side analysis showed small degradation at phone-scale compression.
papers.relevance: Supports linguistically constrained candidate boundaries and confidence-weighted pooling.

papers.title: AdaTranS: Adapting with Boundary-based Shrinking for End-to-End Speech Translation
papers.authors: Xingshan Zeng, Liangyou Li, Qun Liu
papers.problem: Reduce the speech-text length mismatch while retaining informative acoustic content.
papers.method: Predict boundaries, apply weighted shrinking, add alignment losses, and force the training-time number of segments to equal the target transcript length.
papers.results: Improved quality, speed, and memory over other shrinking methods; ablations show count forcing and weighted pooling matter.
papers.relevance: Offers a practical exact-rate supervised warm-up before using a free learned policy at inference.

papers.title: CJST: CTC Compressor based Joint Speech and Text Training for Decoder-Only ASR
papers.authors: Wei Zhou, Junteng Jia, Leda Sari, Jay Mahadeokar, Ozlem Kalinli
papers.problem: Build a robust, compact CTC-derived acoustic prompt for decoder-only ASR and joint speech-text training.
papers.method: Compare blank removal, repeated-label collapse, combined modes, forced peaky alignment, and CTC class embeddings.
papers.results: A conservative blank-threshold mode reported LibriSpeech WER 2.22/4.94 at prompt/text ratio 1.22; a more compact combined mode reached ratio 1.08 with WER 2.27/5.04.
papers.relevance: Closest decoder-only ASR compressor study; demonstrates a measurable compactness-quality trade-off and robustness benefit from conservative confidence-aware removal.

papers.title: Decoder-only Architecture for Speech Recognition with CTC Prompts and Text Data Augmentation
papers.authors: Emiru Tsunoo, Hayato Futami, Yosuke Kashiwagi, Siddhant Arora, Shinji Watanabe
papers.problem: Use a decoder-only ASR architecture that can also benefit from text-only training.
papers.method: Compress CTC-predicted encoder features into an acoustic prompt that an autoregressive decoder refines.
papers.results: Text augmentation improved over ordinary CTC by 0.3 and 1.4 WER on LibriSpeech test-clean and test-other.
papers.relevance: Shows that a compact CTC prompt can be consumed effectively by a decoder-only model.

papers.title: On decoder-only architecture for speech-to-text and large language model integration
papers.authors: Jian Wu, Yashesh Gaur, Zhuo Chen, Long Zhou, Yimeng Zhu, Tianrui Wang, Jinyu Li, Shujie Liu, Bo Ren, Linquan Liu, Yu Wu
papers.problem: Efficiently map speech into the continuous embedding space of a decoder-only language model.
papers.method: Speech-LLaMA combines a CTC compressor, acoustic encoder, continuous adapter, and LLaMA.
papers.results: Reported competitive multilingual speech-to-text results with a compressed acoustic prefix.
papers.relevance: Establishes the broad architecture and the common pattern of pretraining compression before adapting the LLM interface.

papers.title: Extreme Encoder Output Frame Rate Reduction: Improving Computational Latencies of Large End-to-End Models
papers.authors: Rohit Prabhavalkar, Zhong Meng, Weiran Wang, Adam Stooke, Xingyu Cai, Yanzhang He, Arun Narayanan, Dongseong Hwang, Tara N. Sainath, Pedro J. Moreno
papers.problem: Reduce large-model ASR encoder output rate far below conventional subsampling levels.
papers.method: Insert multiple funnel reduction layers and ablate their placement, pooling, and decoder-side capacity.
papers.results: Reported one encoder output per 2.56 seconds with limited large-scale voice-search degradation and major latency reductions; a richer prediction network recovered much of the extreme-rate loss.
papers.relevance: Shows that extreme compression is possible and shifts more modeling responsibility to the decoder.

papers.title: AdaTS: Adaptive Token Sampling for Efficient Speech Language Models
papers.authors: Sonal Sannigrahi, Giuseppe Attanasio, Andre Martins
papers.problem: Reduce redundant speech tokens presented to a speech language model.
papers.method: Score and merge adjacent similar tokens with learned weights; introduce the sampler during a second stage where the downstream model remains trainable.
papers.results: Reported about 2 times fewer tokens and 40 percent higher inference efficiency with comparable or better ASR, speech QA, and speech translation.
papers.relevance: Modern evidence for constrained merge actions, learned pooling, and compressor-decoder co-adaptation.

papers.title: Length-Adaptive Transformer: Train Once with Length Drop, Use Anytime with Search
papers.problem: Train one Transformer to support many accuracy-efficiency budgets instead of one model per sequence length.
papers.method: LengthDrop stochastically changes intermediate sequence lengths during training, followed by multi-objective budget search.
papers.results: One set of weights supports multiple competitive accuracy-efficiency operating points on NLP tasks.
papers.relevance: Strong non-speech precedent for multi-rate warm-up and stochastic rate augmentation.

papers.title: Transformer-Based ASR Incorporating Time-Reduction Layer and Fine-Tuning with Self-Knowledge Distillation
papers.authors: Md. Akmal Haidar, Chao Xing, Mehdi Rezagholizadeh
papers.problem: Lower Transformer ASR frame rate without sacrificing recognition quality.
papers.method: Add internal time-reduction layers and fine-tune with self-knowledge distillation.
papers.results: Reported improved LibriSpeech efficiency and WER over the authors' Transformer baselines.
papers.relevance: Supports high-rate-teacher to low-rate-student distillation as a practical recovery mechanism.

papers.title: CTC-synchronous Training for Monotonic Attention Model
papers.authors: Hirofumi Inaguma, Masato Mimura, Tatsuya Kawahara
papers.problem: Autoregressive monotonic attention can accumulate alignment errors because future alignment evidence is unavailable.
papers.method: Synchronize expected monotonic-attention boundaries to an auxiliary CTC branch during joint training.
papers.results: Improved TEDLIUM2 and LibriSpeech results, particularly for long utterances.
papers.relevance: Supports the interpretation that boundary drift, not rate alone, can propagate through an autoregressive decoder.

themes: Constrained monotonic compression is generally safer than independent frame selection.
Successful compressors and decoders are usually adapted together.
Output count control and boundary quality are distinct optimization problems.
Extreme compression shifts greater modeling responsibility to the decoder.
Multi-budget exposure and teacher-student distillation are established stabilizers.

gaps.statement: Decoder transfer between exact acoustic-prefix rates has not been cleanly isolated from boundary and pooling changes.
gaps.evidence: Decoder-only compressor papers p8-p12 train multiple interface components together rather than reporting a fixed-boundary cross-rate matrix.

gaps.statement: Changing acoustic-prefix length also changes downstream text-token positions in RoPE-based decoder-only models unless position IDs are controlled.
gaps.evidence: The architectures in p8-p10 use compressed acoustic prefixes, but the surveyed reports do not isolate prefix-position shift from acoustic information loss.

gaps.statement: Plain segment means discard duration and within-segment statistics precisely when segments grow long.
gaps.evidence: Weighted aggregation helps in p6 and p7, while p12 explicitly learns merge weights.

gaps.statement: Utterance-level reward assigned to every source frame has weak local credit assignment.
gaps.evidence: The dominant successful alternatives in p4-p8 and p12 use accumulation, linguistic candidates, forced counts, or local merges.

gaps.statement: A rate-band penalty does not directly solve the stated epsilon-constrained goal of minimum rate at bounded ASR degradation.
gaps.evidence: p1 explicitly trades sequence error against frame rate, while p13 treats quality and efficiency as a Pareto problem.

gaps.statement: Per-utterance rate allocation with tail-risk controls is largely unexplored in decoder-only ASR compression.
gaps.evidence: Reviewed methods predominantly impose shared policies or counts; none reports CVaR-style protection for hard/noisy utterances.
